status: NO WEB PAGES WERE OPENED. The environment this assessment was built in blocked every approved health domain (CDC, NIH/MedlinePlus, WHO, AAP, ACOG, HIV.gov, FDA, HHS and state health departments all returned HTTP 403 from the network proxy). Nothing below is therefore cited as 'accessed'. Each claim is listed as NEEDS VERIFICATION with the kind of page that should confirm it. No statistic, study or URL has been invented: the only numbers in the assessment are in charts labeled 'Fictional data for this activity'.
note: Claims here are deliberately stated at topic level. This file is public, so it does not say which statements are true or false in any individual question. The detailed claims, with the questions that rely on them, are in private/REVIEW_DETAIL.md (delivered to the teacher, not in git).
checkedAgainstDistrictMaterials: The NCCVT Health Curriculum Overview (Family Life and Sexuality, lessons 1 to 3) and the K-12 Health Education Concepts document (Reg. 551) were read. They set the framing: HIV prevention that stresses the benefits of abstinence; barrier, hormonal, and sterilization methods of contraception; consent and respecting personal boundaries. They contain no medical statistics.

claims.topic: Abstinence compared with other prevention methods
claims.claim: How abstinence compares with other methods for preventing sexual transmission of STIs (including HIV) and pregnancy, and the fact that some infections also have non-sexual routes.
claims.basis: Build brief section 2 (prompt-supplied) and district overview, lesson 3.
claims.check: CDC STI prevention page; HIV.gov how HIV spreads

claims.claim: How much condoms reduce the risk of STIs and pregnancy, and the limits of that protection. The assessment uses the wording "greatly reduce but do not eliminate" and no percentages.
claims.check: CDC condom effectiveness page; ACOG patient education on contraception

claims.claim: Whether symptoms can show that someone has an STI, and the role of testing.

claims.claim: How the cause of an STI (bacterial or viral) relates to whether it can be cured or only managed, what is known about HPV, and what the HPV vaccine does.
